IS : 11356 - 1985

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR STYRENE-BUTADIENE RUBBER LATEX

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 22 March 1985, after the draft finalized by the Rubber Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coai and Related Products Division Council. 0.2 The type of latex covered in this standard corresponds to the this number is allotted by the commercially known S-2000 latex; International Institute of Synthetic Rubber Producer's Inc, USA. 0.3 Styrene-butadiene latex is used for tyre cord dipping, compounding adhesives for footwear and paper industry, carpet backings, upholstery and linings for proofed goods like fire fighting hoses, etc. 0.4 In preparation IS0 2006-1974(E) speed mechanical for Standardization. assistance has been derived from of this standard, `Synthetic rubber latex - Determination of high stability' published by the International Organization

0.5 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*.

A-l.1 The rubber portion of a latex is separated by a salt-acid methanol coagulation, dried and massed on a mill. The viscosity of the rubber is measured on a Mooney viscometer.

APPENDIX C [ Table 1, Sl Jvo. ( x ) ]
DETERMINATION C-O. GENERAL C-O.1 The test method given below specifies for the determination of the high-speed mechanical stability of synthetic rubber latex. The test is applicable to synthetic rubber latices which have a viscosity, determined with the L instrument in accordance with IS : 9316 ( Part 2 )-1979* of shall be tested up to 200 mPa s ( 200 cP ). Latices of higher viscosity after dilution to a viscosity of 200 mPa.s ( 200 CP ) or less, provided that such dilution does not reduce the concentration of the latex by more than 10 percent total solids.
NOTE - Dilution of the latex decreases its stability because the balance of free and absorbed soap is changed.

OF MECHANICAL

STABILITY

C-O.2 The duration of stirring shall be so selected that the latex does not increase in temperature to more than 60�C and does not exceed a height The duration of stirring shall be as of 100 mm in the latex container. agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier and shall not be longer In the case of a latex which contains than 30 min or less than 1 min. ammonia, the duration of stirring shall be limited, since loss of ammonia by evaporation during the test may cause additional destabilization. C-O.3 The test does not necessarily indicate the stability of a synthetic rubber latex to high shear stress, for which a rubbing test may be more applicable.

C-l. OUTLINE

OF THE

METHOD

C-l.1 The amount of coagulum formed after stirring of the latex at high speed, is regarded as an inverse measure of the mechanical stability of
the latex. C-2.

REAGENT

5 percent solution of potassium oleate of @H value 10, or, for use with a latex which is coaguIated by potassium oleate solution, 5 percent solution of a synthetic anionic surfactant. C-2.1 Soap Solution C-2.2 C-3.

C-3.3 Test Filter - consisting of a disk of stainless steel wire cloth with an average aperture width of 180 f 15 pm, dried to constant mass and weighed to the nearest 1 mg, firmly clamped between two stainless steel rings of equal internal diameter between 25 and 50 mm. C-4. PROCEDURE

C-4.1 In case viscosity of the latex determined with the L instrument [ according to IS : 9316 ( Part 2 )-1979" ] exceeds 200 mPa.s ( 200 CP ), dilute it to this or a lower value, with an amount of water which reduces the concentration of the latex by not more than 10 percent total solids. C-4.2 Adjust the temperature of the latex to 25 f 3"C, pass it through the preliminary filter ( C-3.2 ) and transfer 50 & 0.5 g to the latex Place the container ( C-3.1.1 ) in position and stir the latex container. at 14 000 f 200 rev/min for 30 min, such that the latex does not increase in temperature to more than 60�C and does not exceed a height of If it is necessary to limit foaming, a paste of 100 mm in the container. a silicone defoamer shall be smeared around the upper portion of the Immediately after the termination of inner surface of the container. stirring, remove the latex container and wash the stirrer shaft and disk free from latex deposits with soap solution. Wet the test filter ( C-3.3 ) with soap solution and pour the latex and washings into the test filter. Use soap solution to ensure quantitative transfer of all latex and deposits
